title: Points of the affine w-localization
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and let $W=A^w$ be the affine w-localization [def-weil-pbc-w-localization]. The points of $\operatorname{Spec}W$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] are pairs $(x,y)$ of prime ideals of $A$ with $y\subseteq x$, and their local rings are $A_y$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. The map to $\operatorname{Spec}A$ sends $(x,y)$ to $y$. The connected components are the fibres of the first-coordinate map to the patch space [def-weil-pbc-w-local] of $\operatorname{Spec}A$, each canonically isomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}A_x$. The closed points $(x,x)$ form a Zariski closed subset homeomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}A$ with the patch topology. In particular, $A\to W$ is faithfully flat [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map] and $\operatorname{Spec}W$ is w-local [def-weil-pbc-w-local].

proof.text: Use the small directed set of all finite constructible partitions and all allowed denominators from [def-weil-pbc-w-localization]; importantly, denominators are not fixed once and for all. Write $B_i=\prod_{E\in\mathcal P_i}A_{f_{i,E}}$. For a prime $q\subset W$, its inverse image in $B_i$ selects exactly one component: the finitely many orthogonal component idempotents sum to $1$, so exactly one is outside the prime (at least one by their sum, at most one by their zero pairwise products). The prime contains every other component and is the inverse image of a prime of the selected factor. Under refinement the selected part must lie in the previously selected part, by the transition formula for these idempotents.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 1: selection of a part at each stage

proof.text:
The selected parts have the finite intersection property: a common refinement selects a nonempty subset of their intersection. Each part is a closed subset of the patch space by its finite Boolean description in [def-weil-pbc-w-local]. Compactness of that space from [lem-weil-pbc-w-local-partition] gives a point $x$ in all of them. It is unique: if two primes differ on $f\in A$, the partition by the nonempty members of $D(f),V(f)$ separates them. Thus every stage selects precisely its part containing $x$. Let $y=q\cap A$. It is prime, since inverse image preserves the defining primality equations. If $f
otin x$, take the partition by $D(f),V(f)$ and denominator $f$ on $D(f)$; If $e$ is that factor's idempotent, its inverse for $f$ gives an element $u$ of the product with $fu=e$. Since $e
otin q$, primality implies $f
otin q\cap A=y$. Hence $y\subseteq x$.

Conversely fix primes $y\subseteq x$. In stage $i$, project to the part $E_i$ containing $x$; since $E_i\subset D(f_{i,E_i})$, its denominator is outside $x$ and hence outside $y$. The universal property [lem-weil-pbc-ring-localization-universal-property] gives $A_{f_{i,E_i}}\to A_y\to\kappa(y)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. These maps from $B_i$ are compatible under refinement, because the chosen part refines the old one and the localization maps agree on $A$. They induce $W\to\kappa(y)$; its kernel is a prime $q_{x,y}$ since the target is a field. Its contraction is $y$, and its selected parts contain $x$. This is inverse to the previous assignment: in a selected factor $a/f^n$ belongs to a prime contracting to $y$ exactly when $a\in y$, since $f$ is a unit. Consequently two primes with the same $(x,y)$ have identical inverse images at every stage and are equal, as every element of $W$ has a stage representative [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise].

source.place: Proof, paragraph 1: converse and uniqueness, written explicitly

proof.text: At $q_{x,y}$, localization of $B_i$ kills the unselected components: each other component idempotent is annihilated by the selected idempotent, which is inverted. The resulting local ring is $(A_{f_{i,E_i}})_{yA_{f_{i,E_i}}}\cong A_y$. Indeed, fractions $a/f^n$ outside that prime have $a\notin y$; localizing therefore inverts exactly the elements required for $A_y$. The mutually inverse maps are supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-localization-universal-property]. Under these identifications every transition map is the identity on $A_y$, since it fixes $A$ and its inverses. The localization-colimit statement [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-localization-at-prime] gives $W_{q_{x,y}}\cong A_y$. The affine stalk identification in [lem-weil-pbc-spec-map-stalk-localization] identifies this with the scheme's local ring.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 1: local rings and canonical transitions

proof.text: For every constructible $E\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}A$, the characteristic vector of $E$ in the partition by $E$ and its complement, with denominators $1$, defines an idempotent $e_E\in W$. Empty parts are omitted; $e_\emptyset=0$ and $e_X=1$. Refinement makes this independent of the presentation and gives $e_{E\cap F}=e_Ee_F$ and $e_{X\setminus E}=1-e_E$. Under the point description, $D(e_E)$ is exactly the set of pairs whose first coordinate lies in $E$. These sets are clopen by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-clopen-idempotent], and constructible sets form a basis of the patch topology by [def-weil-pbc-w-local]. Therefore $\pi:\operatorname{Spec}W\to (\operatorname{Spec}A)_{\rm patch}$, $(x,y)\mapsto x$, is continuous. Distinct fibres are separated by a clopen set $D(e_E)$.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 2: idempotents and the first-coordinate map

proof.text: Fix $x$, and let $J_x$ be the ideal generated by $1-e_E$ for all constructible $E$ containing $x$. Selecting the part containing $x$ and mapping $A_f\to A_x$ at every stage gives a compatible homomorphism $\rho_x:W\to A_x$, by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-localization-universal-property]. It kills $J_x$. It is surjective: for $a/s\in A_x$, refine by $D(s),V(s)$ and choose denominator $s$ on $D(s)$; the tuple $a/s$ on this part and zero on its complement maps to $a/s$. For the kernel, represent $b\in W$ at a stage using [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise]. Modulo $J_x$, it equals its selected coordinate $a/f^n$ multiplied by the corresponding idempotent. If $\rho_x(b)=0$, there is $s\notin x$ with $sa=0$ in $A$ by the fraction equality in [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Refine by $D(s),V(s)$ and multiply all denominators on the $D(s)$ parts by $s$. On the part containing $x$ the selected coordinate becomes zero. Thus $e_Fb=0$ for a constructible $F$ containing $x$, and $b=(1-e_F)b\in J_x$. This proves $W/J_x\cong A_x$.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 2: fibre ring, existence and equality of fractions

proof.text: A prime $q$ contains $J_x$ exactly when its selected part at every partition contains $x$, equivalently when its first coordinate is $x$: $e_E(1-e_E)=0$ and $e_E+(1-e_E)=1$ imply that exactly one of $e_E,1-e_E$ belongs to $q$. Thus $q$ contains the generators of $J_x$ exactly when its first coordinate lies in every constructible neighbourhood of $x$; the $D(f),V(f)$ partitions show that this coordinate is $x$. Primes of $W/J_x$ are precisely the primes of $W$ containing $J_x$, by inverse image along the quotient and passage to the quotient ideal; their basic opens agree with the restrictions of $D(b)$ from $W$. On each such basic open, the ring is $(W/J_x)_{\bar b}=W_b/J_xW_b$: both sides have the universal property of killing $J_x$ and inverting $b$. These identifications commute with restriction because they fix the images of elements of $W$. Therefore the closed fibre $\pi^{-1}(x)$, with its canonical affine scheme structure $\operatorname{Spec}(W/J_x)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], is isomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}A_x$ by step 6. Equivalently it is obtained by inverting all $e_E$ with $x\in E$, since an invertible idempotent equals $1$, and conversely an idempotent equal to $1$ is invertible. Both constructions therefore have the same universal property.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 2: identification of the fibre as an affine scheme

proof.text: The spectrum of the local ring $A_x$ is connected. Its maximal ideal is $xA_x$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]; an open neighbourhood of this point contains a basic open $D(a/s)$ containing it, where $a\notin x$, and $a/s$ is a unit. Such a basic open is the entire spectrum. Thus any partition into two disjoint open subsets has an empty member. Step 7 makes each fibre connected. Any connected subset meeting two fibres would be separated by the clopen set of step 5, a contradiction. Hence the fibres are exactly the connected components.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 2: connectedness and maximality of the fibres

proof.text: Specialization of prime points is inclusion of their ideals: $V(q)$ is the closure of $q$ by the definition of the Zariski closed sets. A specialization cannot change the first coordinate, because the clopen sets $D(e_E)$ separate different coordinates. Inside the closed fibre $\operatorname{Spec}A_x$, the unique closed point is its maximal ideal $xA_x$, namely $(x,x)$. Every $(x,y)$ specializes to $(x,x)$; no $(x,x)$ has a further specialization. Thus the closed points of $\operatorname{Spec}W$ are exactly the diagonal pairs. If $y\subsetneq x$, choose $f\in x\setminus y$. The open $D(e_{V(f)})\cap D(f)$ contains $(x,y)$ and contains no diagonal pair. The union of these opens over all $f\in A$ is precisely the complement of the diagonal, which is therefore closed.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 3: closed points and openness of their complement

proof.text: Identify the diagonal with $\operatorname{Spec}A$ by $x\mapsto(x,x)$. The restriction of $D(e_E)$ is $E$, so its subspace topology contains the patch topology. Conversely represent $b\in W$ by a tuple $(a_E/f_E^{n_E})_E$ in a stage, using [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise]. At $(x,x)$, $b$ is outside the prime exactly when $x$ lies in a part $E$ and $a_E\notin x$. Hence the restriction of $D(b)$ is the finite union $\bigcup_E(E\cap D(a_E))$, a constructible set and a patch open [def-weil-pbc-w-local]. Since basic opens form a basis for the Zariski topology, the two topologies coincide. Each connected component has its unique diagonal closed point by steps 8 and 9, and their set is closed by step 9; these are exactly the w-local conditions.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 3: the topology on diagonal pairs and w-locality

proof.text: The construction [def-weil-pbc-w-localization] presents $W$ as an ind-Zariski, hence ind-etale, $A$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. By [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability], its map is weakly etale, which includes flatness by [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. Its spectrum map sends $(x,y)$ to $y$ by step 3, and is surjective since every prime $x$ is the image of $(x,x)$. The flat-surjective-spectrum criterion [lem-weil-pbc-flat-surjective-spectrum-faithfully-flat] now proves faithful flatness. If $A$ is the zero ring, both spectra and the set of pairs are empty and $W$ is the zero ring (the empty product at its sole partition); the same flat-surjective criterion applies, so this case is included.
